function_v0.doc:
Pay this contract's storage rent without doing anything else.

Takes no auth and names no caller. Topping up rent cannot harm
anyone -- the caller spends their own fee to extend an entry
nobody else is charged for -- and gating it behind a privileged
key would mean a dormant contract could only be rescued by
whoever still held that key.

The internal bumps are lazy on purpose: they act only once an
entry is within [`TTL_THRESHOLD`] of archival, so an ordinary
caller almost never pays rent. The cost of that is a lottery.
When the threshold is finally crossed the whole top-up lands on
whichever transaction is next through the door, and because the
instance bump carries the contract's code entry with it, that is
the largest single entry here. Measured on the roster, whose wasm
is half the size of this one: 21.79 XLM for the transaction that
paid, 0.095 XLM for the next one.

This is the other half of that design. A keeper calling `bump`
tops the entries back up whatever their remaining life, so the
cost tracks h
function_v0.name: bump

function_v0.doc:
Transfer ownership of a spend-mode token: move the owner pointer to
`new_owner_commitment`, burning the current owner's claim.

`caller.require_auth()` covers the tx fee only \xe2\x80\x94 **ownership is proven by
the Ed25519 owner-key signature, not the tx source**, so any funded
account may relay a spend. The current owner signs
`SHA-256(SPEND_AUTH || contract_xdr || slot_id (u32 BE) ||
ephemeral_key || current_commitment || new_commitment ||
spend_nonce (u32 BE))` \xe2\x80\x94 the format in
`docs/architecture/spend-mode.md`, which this must agree with letter
for letter; a signer that signs the digest blind relies on it.

Each field earns its place. Both commitments stop the spend being
replayed against a moved state and stop an observer swapping the
successor; the nonce makes the authorisation good for exactly one
transfer, which the commitments alone do not, because a note that
returns to a commitment it held before reproduces the old digest;
the contract address stops a signature crossing deployments; the
slot is the recor
function_v0.name: spend

function_v0.doc: Dissolve the caller's registered pair. Either member may; the\npartner's record goes too. Returns the former partner.
function_v0.name: unpair

function_v0.doc: The pair `node` is registered in, if any.
function_v0.name: pair_of

function_v0.doc: A print slot, assembled from its core and its draw. `lapsed` says\nthe draw is gone.
function_v0.name: get_slot

function_v0.doc: The selection parameters: beacon, claim window, serve timeout and\nminimum node age.
function_v0.name: selection

function_v0.doc:
Pay one note's storage rent.

A note is persistent entries that nothing touches between
`register_token` and redemption, so a note simply *held* for
longer than [`TTL_EXTEND`] is archived while its holder does
nothing wrong. Protocol 23 restores it automatically, but hands
the restore fee to whoever next touches the entry -- the holder,
at redemption, which is the worst possible moment to surprise
someone holding a bearer instrument.

A wallet can call this instead, for the price of the days that
have passed. No auth, for the same reason as [`Self::bump`], and
one more: the holder of a bearer note is not an address this
contract knows, so there is nobody to require auth *from*.

The contract's own entries go with it ([`Self::bump_core`]). A
note whose record is live inside a contract whose code or config
has been archived is not redeemable, so paying for one and not
the other buys nothing. With a keeper running, that part is
already paid and costs nothing here.

Returns false if the slot holds neither a print
function_v0.name: bump_token

function_v0.doc:
Claim accrued node fees. Callable by any node holding a positive balance,
at any time \xe2\x80\x94 earnings are decoupled from the redemption moment, so a node
that was offline when its tokens were redeemed still collects when it next
comes online.
function_v0.name: claim_fees

function_v0.doc:
Seed a slot with its beacon round's signature. Anyone may call it:
a BLS signature is unique, so whoever posts it has nothing to
choose, and withholding it only delays the print.

`signature` is the round's G1 signature, uncompressed. A point off
the curve or outside the subgroup traps in the host before any
pairing; a valid point that is not this round's signature is
`BadBeacon`.
function_v0.name: seed_print

function_v0.doc:
Whether this slot has been redeemed.

Informational, and it can lapse: the marker is not bumped, so
once it archives this answers `false` about a note that was
redeemed. Nothing safety-critical rests on it. A holder asking
whether a note can still be cashed is answered by `get_token`,
which returns nothing for a redeemed note and fails closed.
function_v0.name: is_redeemed

function_v0.doc: The ledger a slot was redeemed on, if the marker is still live.
function_v0.name: redeemed_at

function_v0.doc: Accrued, unclaimed node-fee balance for `node` (0 if none).
function_v0.name: accrued_fees

function_v0.doc: All monetary parameters are immutable after construction.\nNo admin keys, no upgrade path, no fund withdrawal.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Path A (pure bearer): redeem by proving knowledge of the composed
ephemeral secret. The holder signs
`SHA-256(domain_tag || contract_xdr || slot_id (u32 BE) ||
ephemeral_key || recipient_xdr)`.

The recipient is in the digest because `require_auth()` does **not**
bind it \xe2\x80\x94 that binds whoever submits the transaction, while the
signature would otherwise be a standalone credential anyone could
reuse. **Rejects spend-mode tokens** \xe2\x80\x94 those must use
[`redeem_by_key_owned`](Self::redeem_by_key_owned).
function_v0.name: redeem_by_key

function_v0.doc:
Register `(node_a, node_b)` as a pair, so it may claim positions on
prints requested from the next ledger on.

Both sign; both must be selectable on the roster and old enough
(`min_node_age`); and each address is in at most one registered
pair, so a set of addresses cannot be re-combined per draw. Returns
the registration ledger.
function_v0.name: register_pair

function_v0.doc: Reserve a slot and escrow the deposit, naming only the depositor's\nown two end pairs. The interior is chosen by the draw:\n`seed_print`, then `claim_position`.
function_v0.name: request_print

function_v0.doc:
Seed a slot the beacon never seeded, once its round has been due for
`fallback_delay` seconds. Anyone may call it, and the seed is fixed
by the slot, so the caller has nothing to choose.

**This keeps issuance alive if drand stops**, for minutes or for
good; without it every print would wait out its window and be
refunded. The price is that the fallback seed is computable from
the request onward: while the beacon is down, a depositor can pick
the moment they request, and so their draw. That buys fee capture,
the same as steering always did (`docs/architecture/
node-selection.md`), never another holder's funds. While the beacon
is up, round `R` is posted long before the fallback opens, so the
fallback is never used.

Everything after the seed is unchanged: claims, the window, and the
forfeit, which treats a fallback-seeded slot as seeded.
function_v0.name: seed_fallback

function_v0.doc:
Replace the selected pair at the next position with the best
runner-up, because it did not confirm within `serve_timeout`.

**The depositor pays one pair's fee, `2 * node_fee`, burned.** The
contract cannot tell a dead node from a depositor who never sent the
extend request, so skipping has to cost something, or it would be a
free way to steer positions toward one's own runners-up. It is
charged from the depositor rather than the escrow, so the escrow
stays equal to the note's face.

Returns the position skipped.
function_v0.name: skip_position

function_v0.doc:
Claim an interior position for the pair `(node_a, node_b)`.

Both members sign: otherwise anyone could enter an honest pair into
a print it never agreed to serve. The score is
computed here from the seed and the pair, so it cannot be chosen,
and a later claim with a lower score displaces a higher one until
selection closes -- being first earns nothing.

Returns the claim's rank, 0 being the lowest score so far.
function_v0.name: claim_position

function_v0.doc:
Path B (pure bearer): redeem by submitting the full signature chain.
On-chain verification of dual Ed25519 signatures + hash chain. Node fees
accrue to participants. **Rejects spend-mode tokens** \xe2\x80\x94 those must use
[`redeem_by_chain_owned`](Self::redeem_by_chain_owned).
function_v0.name: redeem_by_chain

function_v0.doc:
Path A for spend-mode tokens: as [`redeem_by_key`](Self::redeem_by_key),
plus the current owner opens the live `owner_commitment` and signs
`SHA-256(SPEND_REDEEM || contract_xdr || slot_id (u32 BE) ||
ephemeral_key || owner_commitment || spend_nonce (u32 BE) ||
recipient_xdr)`.
function_v0.name: redeem_by_key_owned

function_v0.doc:
Path B for spend-mode tokens: as [`redeem_by_chain`](Self::redeem_by_chain),
plus the current owner opens the live `owner_commitment` and signs
`SHA-256(SPEND_REDEEM || contract_xdr || slot_id (u32 BE) ||
ephemeral_key || owner_commitment || spend_nonce (u32 BE) ||
recipient_xdr)`.
function_v0.name: redeem_by_chain_owned

udt_struct_v0.doc: A pair's claim on a print, ranked by `score`.
udt_struct_v0.name: Claim

fields.doc: `sha256(seed || lower || higher)` over the pair's two addresses'\nXDR, ordered bytewise. Computed by the mint, never supplied.
fields.name: score

fields.doc: Each member's terms, from the roster at claim time.
fields.name: volunteer_a

cases.doc:
A pair whose two nodes are the same address, or a node that
appears in more than one pair of the same print.

A "pair" of one node is not a pair: the two-party construction is
what makes a shard take two parties to produce, and one operator
holding both halves of a link -- or every link -- collapses that
to a single point of trust while still looking like a chain.
cases.name: NodesNotDistinct

cases.doc: This `event_id` has been used by an earlier print.
cases.name: EventIdInUse

cases.doc: The slot's beacon round has not been posted yet.
cases.name: NotSeeded

cases.doc: `seed_print` on a slot that already has its seed.
cases.name: AlreadySeeded

cases.doc: The signature does not verify as the beacon's for this slot's round.
cases.name: BadBeacon

cases.doc: No more claims: selection has closed, or the window has passed\nwith every position filled.
cases.name: ClaimsClosed

cases.doc: The claim list is full and this score is not lower than its last.
cases.name: ClaimNotCompetitive

cases.doc: Interior links wait for selection: the window has not passed, or\nfewer pairs than positions have claimed.
cases.name: SelectionNotReady

cases.doc: Every runner-up has been used.
cases.name: NoBackup

cases.doc: `seed_fallback` before the slot's round has been due for\n`fallback_delay` seconds.
cases.name: FallbackNotReady

cases.doc:
A record already exists for this slot.

**Unreachable in practice, and kept deliberately.** Registration
must never write over an existing entry: `ephemeral_key` is the
sum of the partial public keys `confirm_link` publishes, so anyone
watching the ledger can compute one.

Records are keyed by **slot**, and `register_token` requires a
`Printing` slot and deletes it, so a second registration is
refused as `SlotNotFound` before this check runs. The check stays because it
guards the nullifier directly instead of relying on an invariant
about a different key.

Note what is *not* prevented: a redeemed `ephemeral_key` can be
registered again under a **new slot**. That is a separate record
with its own escrow, and it takes nothing from the first.
cases.name: TokenExists

cases.doc:
A payout or a participant slot named this contract.

The escrow would leave the books and arrive back in the same
balance with nothing recording that it is owed to anyone -- not
stolen, but unreachable, and the note consumed.
cases.name: PayoutToSelf

cases.doc:
The constructor was given parameters no print could ever satisfy.

A mint is immutable, so a deployment that cannot mint is permanent:
the only remedy is to deploy again and tell everyone the old address
is dead. Rejecting at construction is the one chance to catch it.
cases.name: InvalidConfig

cases.doc: The pair at this position has not yet had `serve_timeout` ledgers.
cases.name: ServeTimeoutNotReached

cases.doc: Only the next interior position can be skipped.
cases.name: NotSkippable

cases.doc: A member of the pair joined the roster less than `min_node_age`\nledgers ago.
cases.name: NodeTooNew

cases.doc: One of the addresses is already in a registered pair; `unpair` first.
cases.name: AlreadyPaired

cases.doc: The caller is in no registered pair.
cases.name: NotPaired

cases.doc: The claim is not a pair registered before this slot was requested.
cases.name: PairNotRegistered

cases.doc:
The slot's draw (`DataKey::Draw`) has lapsed while the slot is
still inside its window. Reachable only on a mint whose window is
longer than the network's `max_entry_ttl`, after that long with no
write. Cancel still settles it.
cases.name: DrawLapsed

tuple_v0.doc:
A registered note, keyed by the **slot** that produced it.

Not keyed by `ephemeral_key`: that is a caller-named value that is
public before its owner registers it (`confirm_link` publishes the
partial keys, and `ek` is their sum). With registration refusing to
overwrite, an `ek` key would make it "first to name the key wins":
anyone with a parked completed slot could claim a victim's key the
moment it became computable, and the victim's print could never be
registered at all.

A slot id is issued by the contract, not chosen by a caller, so
two prints cannot collide. Two slots naming the same `ek`
are simply two records: each has its own escrow, chain hash and
claim key, and a squatter only puts their own deposit within
reach of whoever holds that key.
tuple_v0.name: Token

tuple_v0.doc: Claimable node-fee balance for a node address (churn-tolerant earnings).\nCredited at redemption (both paths), drained by `claim_fees`.
tuple_v0.name: Accrued

tuple_v0.doc:
Marks an `event_id` as spent, so no second print can claim it.

The chain hash already binds a chain to its token, so this is not the thing standing between a forged chain and an
escrow -- but an `event_id` is how every off-chain party names a
print, and two prints answering to one name is a reconciliation
problem nobody can fix after the fact. Written once per print and
never removed.
tuple_v0.name: EventIdUsed

tuple_v0.doc:
A redeemed slot, and the ledger it was redeemed on.

This replaces the whole `TokenRecord` once a note is paid out.
The record is not needed as the nullifier: a second redemption is refused because
the record it needs is *absent*, not because it is present and
says `Redeemed`. Slot ids come from `NextSlotId` and are never
reused, so a deleted slot can never be resurrected -- the
counter is the nullifier, and the ~450-byte record would only pay
rent to restate what the counter already guarantees.

What the marker buys back is the difference between "redeemed"
and "never existed", which absence alone cannot express. It is
deliberately *not* bumped: on-chain reads restore it
automatically when a redemption attempt names it, so refusing a
double-redeem stays correct forever, while the off-ledger
convenience of `is_redeemed` lapses when it archives. Safety
does not rest on it -- a holder asking "can I redeem this?" is
answered by `get_token` returning nothing.
tuple_v0.name: Redeemed

tuple_v0.doc:
The pair an address is registered in, and when (`register_pair`).

Pairs are fixed before a draw so an operator cannot choose which of
its addresses to combine after the seed is public: a score is a hash
of the combination, so free re-pairing let `n` staked addresses try
`n(n-1)/2` pairings against every seed.
tuple_v0.name: PairOf

tuple_v0.doc:
The growing half of a print slot, in **temporary** storage
(`docs/architecture/node-selection.md`, "Where a slot lives"): its
pairs, seed, claims, partial keys and confirmers. `Slot(id)` keeps the escrow and every
fixed-size fact, and never changes size after `request_print`.

Rent is charged on an entry's growth for its whole remaining life,
and a persistent entry lives at least 120 days on mainnet whatever
the contract asks. Kept on the slot, a claim would cost a node
~0.045 XLM; here it rents at the temporary rate for the print window.
tuple_v0.name: Draw

udt_struct_v0.doc:
What `DataKey::Slot` stores: the escrow and every fixed-size fact of a
print. Written at `request_print` and rewritten at the **same size**
after, so its 120-day mainnet rent is paid once, by the depositor.
Assembled with [`SlotDraw`] into the
[`PrintSlot`] every reader sees.
udt_struct_v0.name: SlotCore

fields.doc: 0 until seeded, so it also says whether the slot was seeded.
fields.name: claim_deadline

udt_struct_v0.doc: What `DataKey::Draw` stores, in temporary storage: the parts of a\nprint that grow as it is selected and built.
udt_struct_v0.name: SlotDraw

fields.doc: The beacon round that seeds this slot, fixed at request.
fields.name: beacon_round

fields.doc: The last ledger of the claim window; 0 until seeded.
fields.name: claim_deadline

fields.doc: Before closing: every competitive claim, lowest score first,\ncapped at `2k`. After: the runners-up only, in the order they\nreplace skipped pairs.
fields.name: claims

fields.doc: Whether the interior positions are fixed (`pairs` is complete).
fields.name: closed

fields.doc:
Who confirmed each link, in link order.

`confirm_link` accepts either member of the assigned pair, and a
shard is derivable by one of them alone -- so "this pair worked"
is not something the chain can see. Only "this address
confirmed" is. Abandoned-slot settlement pays the confirmer and
nobody else, because that is the whole of what is provable.
fields.name: confirmers

fields.doc: Whether the claim list ever held `k` claims. It never shrinks below\n`k` before closing, so this is the one fact about the claims the\nforfeit needs, kept where it outlives the draw.
fields.name: filled

fields.doc:
The draw (`DataKey::Draw`) has lapsed: `pairs` holds only the end
pairs and `seed`, `claims`, `partial_keys` and `confirmers` are
empty because they are gone, not because nothing happened. Only
settlement works on such a slot.
fields.name: lapsed

fields.doc: The ledger the current position became current: when selection\nclosed, or when the previous link was confirmed or skipped. A skip\nis allowed `serve_timeout` ledgers after it.
fields.name: last_progress

fields.doc:
The pairs in chain order, once selection closes.

Until then it holds only the depositor's two end pairs,
`[first, last]`: the interior positions are nobody's to name
until the draw is in. Closing
inserts the `k` winning claims between them, and a skip replaces
one interior entry with a runner-up.
fields.name: pairs

fields.doc:
Each confirmed link's partial public key, in link order.

**Published, not checked.** Nothing on-chain reads these: Soroban
exposes no Curve25519 point addition, so the contract cannot sum
them and compare against the `ephemeral_key` a depositor supplies
to `register_token`. They are here so that anyone watching the
ledger can do that sum themselves and confirm the key a note
claims is the key its construction produced.

They are therefore evidence for observers, not a constraint on
the depositor. Their presence in the slot is not a binding, and
an on-chain reader must not treat it as one.
fields.name: partial_keys

fields.doc: Set by `seed_print` from that round's verified signature.
fields.name: seed

fields.doc:
Which participants volunteer: bit `2i` is pair `i`'s `node_a`,
bit `2i + 1` its `node_b`, the same order as
`TokenRecord::participants`. A volunteer's fees are burned, not
credited.

Taken from the roster's `node_terms` once, when the pair claims
(recorded in its [`Claim`]), and set here when selection closes or
a skip brings in a runner-up. A node is paid on the terms it had
when it claimed, and nothing after the print has to consult the
roster. End pairs are never set: they are the depositor's and draw
no fee.
`MAX_REDEEMABLE_PAIRS = 12` is 24 participants, inside a `u32`.
fields.name: volunteers

udt_struct_v0.doc: The depositor skipped a selected pair that did not serve, and a\nrunner-up took its place. `fee` is what the depositor paid to do it,\nburned.
udt_struct_v0.name: SkipEvent

udt_enum_v0.doc:
Per-token spend mode, fixed at `register_token`. See
`docs/architecture/spend-mode.md`.

- `PureBearer` \xe2\x80\x94 whoever holds the bytes can redeem;
`owner_commitment` is unused.
- `Spend` \xe2\x80\x94 an on-ledger owner pointer (`owner_commitment`) that the current
owner moves via `spend` (burning their claim) and that redemption requires
opening (the owner-checked redeem paths). Prevents payer double-spend.
udt_enum_v0.name: TokenMode

udt_struct_v0.doc: A claim was accepted at `rank` (0 is the lowest score so far).
udt_struct_v0.name: ClaimEvent

fields.doc: How interior pairs are chosen.
fields.name: selection

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The roster's `Node` record, as `get_node` returns it, read here only
for `joined_at` (`min_node_age`).

A `contracttype` struct crosses contracts as a map keyed by field
name, so this must name the same fields with the same types as
`kenter-roster`'s `Node`. The roster is immutable, so it cannot drift
under a deployed mint; `test::the_mock_roster_node_matches` and the
system test against the real roster are what catch a mismatch here.
udt_struct_v0.name: RosterNode

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Emitted on a spend-mode ownership transfer. Endpoints are opaque commitments;
an observer can see the token changed hands but not who to. Successive
spends of one token are linkable to each other; that per-token linkage
is accepted (see `docs/architecture/spend-mode.md`).
udt_struct_v0.name: SpendEvent

fields.doc: Which record moved. The key alone does not identify one.
fields.name: slot_id

fields.doc: The nonce **after** this spend. An observer rebuilding owner\nhistory from events needs it to know where the next\nauthorisation has to be made.
fields.name: spend_nonce

fields.doc:
SHA-256 of the canonical Path-B `chain_data` blob, committed by the
depositor at registration. Binds redemption to the real signed chain so
a chain cannot be forged from public data (see
`docs/architecture/security-model.md`).
fields.name: chain_hash

fields.doc:
Public half of the note's **claim key**, fixed at registration.

The secret half travels inside the note container and is never sent
to this contract. Path B redemption presents a signature from it
rather than the chain preimage alone, which is what stops a
redemption being lifted out of the ledger: `chain_data` is published
by any attempt, successful or failed, and a failed one leaves the
note Active with its secret in public view.

This does not make the note non-bearer. The key is in the file, not
tied to a person: copy the file and you copy the right to redeem.
Spend mode is the opposite trade and is already recipient-bound, so
it does not need one.
fields.name: claim_pubkey

fields.doc: Spend mode for this token (fixed at registration).
fields.name: mode

fields.doc: The current owner commitment `SHA-256("kntr_v1:spend:owner" || owner_pubkey)`.\nOverwritten each `spend`. Unused (and unchecked) when `mode == PureBearer`.
fields.name: owner_commitment

fields.doc:
How many times this note has been spent on. Part of both owner
digests, so a signature is good for exactly one transfer.

Without it the digest would be `(ek, current_commitment,
new_commitment)`, which repeats whenever a note returns to an
owner commitment it held before \xe2\x80\x94 and the static pay tag (owner
index 0) is a reusable address, so a note coming back as change
or a refund does exactly that. The earlier signature would then
replay, and a former payee could take the note back.
fields.name: spend_nonce

fields.doc: Copied from the slot: which `participants` volunteer. See\n[`PrintSlot::volunteers`].
fields.name: volunteers

udt_struct_v0.doc: Positions abandoned after a draw, burned out of the escrow at cancel or\nexpiry.
udt_struct_v0.name: ForfeitEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A volunteer's fee, destroyed instead of credited.

One per volunteer per settlement, redemption included, so anyone can
check from events alone that a volunteer was never paid for the
settlements it volunteered on.

Terms are per address and fixed when a print is requested. An
address that volunteered from its first join is never credited, so
its `Accrued` balance stays at zero. One that converted keeps what it
accrued while paid, and is still credited by prints requested before
it converted.

If the pay token refused the burn, the settlement also emits a
[`FeeLockedEvent`]: the amount stayed in the mint instead, where
nothing can move it.
udt_struct_v0.name: FeeBurnedEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The pay token refused a settlement's burn, so the volunteers' fees
(`amount`, the settlement's total) stay in the mint's balance. No
entry point can move them: they are no node's `Accrued` and no slot's
escrow, so they are as unreachable as burned. A burn that traps
would instead have locked the holder's payout or the depositor's
refund forever.
udt_struct_v0.name: FeeLockedEvent

fields.doc: The ledger the pair was registered in. A pair may claim only on\nslots requested after it.
fields.name: registered_at

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Emitted once per confirmer credited by an abandoned print.

Redemption reports its payouts in aggregate on the `Redeem*` events.
Without this, settling a cancelled or expired slot would publish
nothing, and a node that had earned a fee could learn of it only by
polling `get_accrued` against every slot it ever touched. The amount is what this settlement credited, not the running
balance.
udt_struct_v0.name: FeeAccruedEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc:
How nodes select themselves into a print
(`docs/architecture/node-selection.md`).

Immutable, like the rest of the config. The beacon fields name a drand
chain of scheme `bls-unchained-g1-rfc9380` (quicknet). The scheme
itself -- hash-to-curve DST, signature group, message -- is fixed in
the contract, so only the chain's own constants are parameters.
udt_struct_v0.name: SelectionConfig

fields.doc: Unix time of the beacon's round 1.
fields.name: beacon_genesis

fields.doc: Rounds between a request and the round that seeds it. The round\n`round_at(request time) + beacon_lead` must not exist yet when the\nrequest lands, or a depositor could know the draw in advance.
fields.name: beacon_lead

fields.doc: Seconds between rounds.
fields.name: beacon_period

fields.doc: The beacon's group key: G2, uncompressed (Soroban's encoding).
fields.name: beacon_pk

fields.doc: Ledgers after `seed_print` during which a lower score may still\ndisplace a higher one.
fields.name: claim_window

fields.doc: Seconds after round `R` is due before `seed_fallback` may seed a\nslot nobody has seeded from the beacon. At least\n`MIN_FALLBACK_DELAY`.
fields.name: fallback_delay

fields.doc: Ledgers a node must have been on the roster before it may claim\n0 turns the check off.
fields.name: min_node_age

udt_struct_v0.doc: The slot is seeded: pairs may claim until `claim_deadline`.
udt_struct_v0.name: PrintSeededEvent

fields.doc: Interior positions to fill (`k`).
fields.name: positions

fields.doc:
Who submitted the transaction.

**Not who was paid.** `redeem_*` takes a separate `recipient`, so
an indexer reading this as the payee is wrong every time the two
differ -- which is the ordinary case for a redemption directed
anywhere but the submitter's own account.
fields.name: holder

fields.doc: Total node fees credited to participants' accrual balances (claimable\nvia `claim_fees`), not paid instantly.
fields.name: node_fees_accrued

fields.doc: Volunteers' fees, burned. `amount + node_fees_accrued +\nnode_fees_burned` is the escrow.
fields.name: node_fees_burned

fields.doc: Who the escrow was actually paid to.
fields.name: recipient

fields.doc:
Which record was redeemed.

The key does not identify one: records are keyed by slot, so two
may legitimately name the same `ephemeral_key`. `TokenActive` and
`Spend` carry it too; the redemption events need it most, since
they are the ones that say where the money went.
fields.name: slot_id

fields.doc: As on `PrintCancelledEvent`.
fields.name: burned

fields.doc: As on `PrintCancelledEvent`: the settled part of the deposit.
fields.name: earned

fields.doc: As on `PrintCancelledEvent`.
fields.name: forfeited

fields.doc: The **gross** escrow. Node fees come off it at redemption, so\nthis is not the figure a `Redeem*` event reports.
fields.name: amount

fields.doc:
The chain commitment, and the claim key.

Without these an indexer following events alone cannot tell
which note a given `ephemeral_key` belongs to \xe2\x80\x94 and since
records are keyed by slot, two of them may legitimately name
the same key.
fields.name: chain_hash

fields.doc: Who registered it.
fields.name: depositor

fields.doc: Spend mode, fixed at registration.
fields.name: mode

fields.doc: The beacon round whose signature will seed the slot.
fields.name: beacon_round

fields.doc: The depositor's own end pairs. The interior is chosen by the draw.
fields.name: first_pair

udt_struct_v0.doc: The slot was seeded by `seed_fallback` rather than the beacon. Published\nbeside the ordinary `seeded` event, which carries the seed.
udt_struct_v0.name: PrintFallbackEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc: Selection closed: `pairs` is the chain, end pairs included.
udt_struct_v0.name: PrintSelectedEvent

fields.doc: Who submitted the transaction. **Not who was paid** -- see\n[`RedeemByKeyEvent::holder`].
fields.name: holder

fields.doc: Total node fees credited to participants' accrual balances, claimable\nvia `claim_fees`. Safe on Path B because the chain hash binds\nredemption to the real chain.
fields.name: node_fees_accrued

fields.doc: Volunteers' fees, burned -- see [`RedeemByKeyEvent::node_fees_burned`].
fields.name: node_fees_burned

fields.doc: Who the escrow was actually paid to.
fields.name: recipient

fields.doc: Which record was redeemed \xe2\x80\x94 see [`RedeemByKeyEvent::slot_id`].
fields.name: slot_id

fields.doc: Volunteer confirmers' fees, destroyed rather than paid.
fields.name: burned

fields.doc: What the confirmers were paid out of the deposit. `refund +\nearned + burned` is the whole of it, which is the check a\ndepositor following events needs.
fields.name: earned

fields.doc: Abandoned positions' fees, burned.\n`refund + earned + burned + forfeited` is the deposit.
fields.name: forfeited
